summary.one_liner: PyApp is a Rust-based wrapper that packages a Python application into a standalone binary which bootstraps itself at runtime.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes PyApp as a wrapper for Python applications that bootstrap themselves at runtime. It is aimed at building standalone binaries for every platform. It offers optional management commands, such as self updates, and the README says its runtime behavior is highly configurable so different end users can be targeted. Documentation is built with Material for MkDocs and hosted on GitHub Pages. The README gives little detail beyond these points and does not include install or build commands.
use_cases: distribute a Python CLI as a standalone binary
build platform-specific executables for Python apps
add self-update to a Python application
bootstrap a Python app at first run for end users
notable: Builds standalone binaries for every platform from a Python application
Optional management commands such as self updates
Runtime behavior is highly configurable for different end users
caveats: README gives no install or build steps; details are in the external documentation
Relies on the docs site for the detailed walkthrough and configuration
